Why the tide table lies

Published tide tables predict the astronomical tide, which assumes still air and an average sea-level pressure. Real harbours rarely oblige.

A deep low-pressure system can lift the sea by half a metre; a strong onshore wind can add another quarter. Skippers who trust the printed height of water alone have run aground in a "high tide".

The practical rule is simple: take the tabulated height, subtract one centimetre per millibar of pressure above 1013, and keep a generous margin under the keel. The data in this article is free for everyone to read in full.
